Gaza City, Gaza Strip A young boy, who had his left hand amputated after being injured in an Israeli strike that killed his father, mother and sisters, writes in his notebook in a tent he shares with his grandmother.
Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine Rescuers extinguish a fire at a shopping centre which broke out after a Russian overnight drone attack.

Manila, Philippines Police are deployed along the road leading to the presidential palace in anticipation of anti-corruption protests that will also mark the 54th anniversary of the declaration of martial law by the late dictator Ferdinand Marcos Sr, father of the current president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
Children in 1950s-style pedal cars race past a large audience of spectators at a racetrack.

Beijing, China Workers in Tiananmen Square assemble a display of giant artificial flowers in the run-up to China’s National Day on 1 October.
Warsaw, Poland ‘Tram bowling’ at the European TramDriver Championship, a one-day test of tram drivers’ skills won this year by a team from Prague.
Havana, Cuba A man stands in the street during a widespread power cut, at least the sixth major outage in Cuba this year.

Gaza City, Palestine A mural on part of a destroyed building thanks the US rapper Macklemore for voicing support for Palestinians, after he was dropped from Ed Sheeran’s tour.
Milan, Italy More than 90 performers on stage at La Scala in a revival of the lavish 1990 staging of Verdi’s La Traviata.

Tegucigalpa, Honduras A Garifuna woman campaigns for Honduras to comply with rulings by the inter-American court of human rights protecting her community’s ancestral lands, after an international delegation urged the same.

St Petersburg, Russia Workers remove the coat of arms from Germany’s consulate general, which Moscow ordered closed in response to Germany shutting Russia’s diplomatic mission in Bonn.
Madhya Pradesh state, India Campaigners lie on symbolic funeral pyres to protest against the Ken-Betwa river link project, which they say will submerge villages and displace communities.
London, UK A model at London fashion week wears clothes from the Chinese designer Yuhan Wang’s 2027 spring/summer collection.
Police escort residents past debris outside a residential building.

Gaza Strip Displaced Palestinians shelter in a heavily damaged building in Gaza City. According to the territory’s health ministry, 1,369 Palestinians have been killed and 4,627 wounded since a fragile ceasefire took effect on 11 October 2025.

Gaza Strip Palestinian fishers depart from Gaza City’s damaged seaport. Benjamin Netanyahu said this week that he would seek new laws allowing Israel to strip citizenship from people who ‘smear’ Israeli soldiers, escalating the campaign against the Oscar-winning film-makers behind the documentary NAZA , who have faced threats from senior government and military officials and far-right groups gathering outside their families’ homes.

Homesh, West Bank A young Israeli settler carries a toy gun during the inauguration of a new synagogue. An Israeli soldier shot a Palestinian man this week , wounding him in the leg, as settlers confronted villagers by grazing livestock on Palestinian land in the town of Faqqua. The incident is the latest to raise questions over the Israeli government’s ability or willingness to curb violent settlers in the occupied West Bank, where attacks have continued to increase.

Al-Tuwani, West Bank Arwa Amr brushes her daughter Layan’s hair as they prepare for school inside the cave that the family has turned into their home. Israel is working towards the systematic ‘elimination’ of the conditions that sustain Palestinian collective life in the occupied West Bank, according to a major report published by the human rights group B’Tselem.

Tehran, Iran Female militia members take part in a military march. As the US war with Iran drags on, the number of Republicans signalling that the conflict is a liability for their party continues to grow.

Arabian Sea A sailor handles munitions on the flight deck of the USS George Washington. The US House of Representatives has voted for a third time to end the war in Iran, approving a resolution a few hours after a Congressional Budget Office report showed the conflict had cost at least $38bn and left the US stockpile of defensive missiles so depleted it could take five years to replenish.

Aden, Yemen Displaced Yemenis rest at a temporary shelter after fleeing Houthi attacks in Al-Khawkhah and Mocha. Abandoning their homes and cramming into cars, thousands of Yemeni families have fled a lightning advance of rebel fighters along the Red Sea coastal plains. People have moved up the rugged hills towards the mountaintop city of Taiz as the war returned in dramatic form this month.

Kyiv, Ukraine A fire burns at a warehouse complex after debris from a Russian drone fell in the district of Sviatoshynskyi. Russian missiles and drones injured at least 19 people in Ukraine’s capital and the surrounding region, authorities said on Thursday. Kyiv’s military administration said more than 10 locations were hit and 33 sites damaged in the wider region.

Nairobi, Kenya Supporters of the opposition Linda Mwananchi movement take part in a rally. Edwin Sifuna has emerged as the loudest threat to President William Ruto’s push for re-election in August 2027. Sifuna has built momentum by tapping into widespread anger over corruption and political violence.

Pristina, Kosovo Kosovo Albanians take part in a rally to call for the acquittal of the former president Hashim Thaçi on the day he was sentenced at a trial in The Hague. Thaçi was jailed for 25 years for war crimes , including dozens of murders, committed as a senior commander of the Kosovo Liberation Army during the country’s war for independence from Serbia in the late 1990s.

Pristina, Kosovo Riot police stand guard as people protest outside the Eulex headquarters after Hashim Thaçi and three former guerrilla commanders were convicted of 96 murders, as well as torture, cruel treatment and arbitrary detention directed at political opponents and civilians.
Santiago, Chile Carabineros detain a woman during a march for the victims of Augusto Pinochet’s dictatorship marking the 53rd anniversary of the coup that brought him to power.

Frontignan, France Police officers intervene as French fishers block access to an oil depot. Mediterranean fishers have launched an indefinite strike in the south of France to protest against the surging cost of marine diesel and a deterioration in their working conditions.
Nu’man, Syria A displaced man searches for recyclable materials at a rubbish dump. Impoverished people have to rely on scavenging through mountains of waste for plastic and metal to sell.

Durban, South Africa A woman waves goodbye to friends as asylum seekers and refugees board a bus for relocation to the Lindela repatriation centre in Gauteng. Documented refugees from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi and Rwanda have lived on the streets for about four months after fleeing communities where they say they faced hostility, threats and intimidation.
Bukavu, Democratic Republic of the Congo Grieving family members support a man who collapsed during the funerals of children killed in a fire and crush at a school in which at least 26 died.
London, England Jacquelin Harris, Jesse Obremski, Isaiah Day, Ashley Kaylynn Green and Yannick Lebrun perform during the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater’s Legacy/New Works at Sadler’s Wells.

Doonbeg, Ireland Fans watch Ireland’s Shane Lowry putt on the 18th green during the Irish Open at Trump International Golf Links. Donald Trump caused consternation on both sides of the Irish Sea on Saturday when, at the start of a two-day visit to Ireland, he said he would love to see a united Ireland and ‘it may as well happen now’.
New York City Alfie Hewett, of the UK, celebrates defeating Tokito Oda, of Japan, in the men’s wheelchair singles final at the 2026 US Open at Flushing Meadows.
